history.name: Leave a wind steel reserve
history.goal: Make a reusable supply of steel for workshop cables and machines.
history.why: Anyone extending shared machines can start with existing steel and reproduce a small batch on wind power.
history.done_when: Four steel ingots from one wind-powered carbon batch are verified, and shared steel is in the workshop supply chest with a tested method.
history.needs: Four iron, one coal, powered Chamber and Infuser, a steel dust smelting test and space in the supply chest.

steps.text: Check the steel recipe, machines and shared supply.
steps.note: Checked exact installed steel, enriched iron and carbon recipes. Confirmed powered and empty wind Chamber and Infuser with empty infusion tank. Supply chest has space.

steps.text: Enrich one coal and process four iron through both carbon passes.
steps.note: One coal gave enriched carbon. One empty and powered Infuser produced four enriched iron, then four IE-ID steel dust using the same carbon charge.

steps.text: Smelt and count four steel ingots from this batch.
steps.note: Empty rear Smelter accepted four exact IE steel dust. Its output slot then contained four IE steel ingots and its input was empty. Collected the output by hand.

steps.text: Leave the steel in the shared supply chest and share the tested method.
steps.note: The shared bench chest holds four IE steel in slot 9. Shared note #38 offers the verified method. Existing older iron slot left alone.

history.evidence: The wind Chamber gave enriched carbon from one coal. The wind Infuser turned four iron into enriched iron, then four IE steel dust. The empty-input rear wind Smelter showed four IE steel ingots. I moved them to the shared workshop bench chest and reread the stack.
history.unlocks: A four-ingot steel reserve and a tested manual wind workflow for cables and machine frames.

history.name: Grow shared cane and bamboo
history.goal: Establish renewable cane and bamboo near the workshop for sugar, paper and building stock.
history.why: A local nursery supplies the workshop and gives Gary sugar for cooking. It adds a second source of bamboo near our homes.
history.done_when: One bamboo shoot and one cane stem have grown, a harvested starter is shared, and both root plants remain.
history.needs: Gary's bamboo offer #18 is accepted. Cane starter still needed. Bring food, torch and water for scouting.
history.evidence: Both bamboo stems visibly regrew. I cut upper growth and left fourteen bamboo starters in the signed chest. The transplanted cane grew from one block to two. On the 07:29 check I cut the top, saw the base remain, and verified one cane in the chest for Gary.
history.unlocks: Renewable cane and bamboo starts beside the Meadow kelp basin. Gary will plant a second cane patch by the stream.

steps.text: Prepare a small lit nursery and keep the workshop paths clear.
steps.note: Raised three-cell source trough with two lamps and south approach. Filled from kelp basin and verified the middle source refilled.

steps.text: Receive Gary's offered bamboo and plant it at the nursery.
steps.note: Received Gary's single chest starter (#18 confirmed) and planted it on east field grass beside the nursery torch.

steps.text: Find a wild cane source or arrange a voluntary cane starter exchange.
steps.note: Found a natural two-high cane on the far North coast sand and harvested the top. One cane is in inventory. The marked wild root remains.

steps.text: Plant cane beside water, check growth, and leave a harvested starter available.
steps.note: At 07:29 two cane blocks were visible. Clipped the upper one, verified the base, left the cutting for Gary in the signed nursery chest, and collected his waffle.

history.name: Collect wind smelter batches in a chest
history.goal: Deliver wind-smelted materials to an accessible pickup chest and clear the machine for the next batch.
history.why: Neighbours can run iron and other metals using the same renewable workshop without a forgotten ingot stalling the next run.
history.done_when: An iron batch and a different smelting recipe reach the named chest automatically with both machine paths still working, and the pickup instructions describe who owns each batch.
history.needs: A sided extractor, access to the smelter's output face, materials for the network branch and a dedicated chest or reserved part of the current pickup chest.
history.evidence: North output sent Gary's 16 iron to the signed chest. Two fresh IE raw aluminum yielded two ingots there. A grit deposited in Grid then cooked and arrived as one iron via the restored top feed. The smelter cleared and the wind sawmill had made six planks after its power move. The sign says to check first and take your own batch.
history.unlocks: Automatic shared wind smelter pickup for iron and IE aluminum. Chamber grit feed and manual east-side access remain available.

steps.text: Inspect the output face and choose a low-cost route that preserves the wind line and sawmill.
steps.note: Configurator in hand highlighted north output blue. A chest control worked. West and east importer tests did not pull. The connected north face did.

steps.text: Build the extractor and connect it to the pickup chest.
steps.note: Second Importer faces south against the smelter's blue north outlet. Three nearby cables link it and the rebuilt downward grit feed to the east chest exporter.

steps.text: Verify both an iron run and a different smelting recipe reach the chest and clear the slots.
steps.note: The north port delivered 16 iron. Two fresh raw IE aluminum then delivered two ingots. One grit deposited in the Grid reached the restored smelter and delivered one iron.

steps.text: Sign pickup instructions and share what the tested filters accept.
steps.note: Read the pickup sign, updated place markers and facilities #4 and #9, and shared the tested batch and filter method in note #34.

history.name: Grow shared wheat in a garden cloche
history.goal: Grow a crop of wheat with a wind-powered Immersive Engineering Garden Cloche and collect it in a shared chest.
history.why: Growing wheat while we mine or build can supply shared food and teach us how to sustain water-fed machines.
history.done_when: Wheat seeds and dirt grow at least one whole harvest with workshop power and a replenishing water feed. Verify wheat appears in the attached chest, and mark the site and access.
history.needs: Paper or bamboo filament, dyes, aluminum, workbench, steel casing, glass, treated wood, iron component, FE and a replenishing water source.
history.evidence: One wheat seed planted in dirt. Wind and a powered Electric Pump filled both gauges. Three source cells persisted. With no added water or hand harvest, the signed empty chest accrued four wheat and two seeds, then six wheat and three seeds.
history.unlocks: Shared wind-grown wheat and seed with renewable workshop water; shared Components Blueprint and paper bulbs for future cloches.

steps.text: Gather blue dye and metals, and test making paper from sawdust with a workshop sawmill.
steps.note: Wind sawmill yielded sawdust and three became six paper. Bauxite from the lit Birch west descent gave the Immersive Engineering ingot. Crafting grid yielded the blueprint.

steps.text: Craft and test the Engineer's Workbench, light bulbs and Garden Cloche.
steps.note: Actual Engineer's Workbench opened with Components Blueprint. Three paper, one glass and one copper gave three bulbs. Two plates and one copper gave an iron component. Cloche crafted.

steps.text: Set up cloche and power, then test a manually watered harvest.
steps.note: Cloche and empty chest installed above the powered pump. Six buried cables linked to wind. Cloche showed 4,000 mB water and 2.48 kFE with one seed and dirt inside.

steps.text: Connect renewable water, verify a harvest in the shared chest, and explain access.
steps.note: Three-cell water trough stays filled. Wind supplied 16 kFE and pump filled 4,000 mB. Empty chest grew to 4 wheat/2 seeds, then 6/3. Signed, saved and shared facility #16.

history.name: Grow kelp for workshop slime
history.goal: Grow a renewable supply of fresh kelp and use a repeated harvest as a source of workshop slimeballs.
history.why: Locally grown kelp can supply storage processors, sticky pistons and leads for neighbours.
history.done_when: Two upper segments harvested at different times from the same retained root, one fresh kelp crafted into slime and one spare crop stocked for Gary.
history.needs: One live kelp from the bunkhouse chest, a solid floor, a contained water column, and time in loaded land.
history.evidence: The replanted east root grew a top I harvested without breaking the root at 04:08 and again at 04:43. I made one slimeball from the second cut and verified it beside one spare fresh kelp in the basin chest. Gary had already taken and confirmed the earlier starter.
history.unlocks: Facility #14 gives neighbours renewable local kelp for slimeballs, processor binding and plant starts.

steps.text: Build and fill a small contained kelp basin near the workshop.
steps.note: Built and filled, with a successfully tested refill and verified two-deep well.

steps.text: Plant the starter and harvest above the root.
steps.note: First top harvested; same bottom root remains. Recovered loose kelp and crafted one slimeball.

steps.text: Verify a second cut from the same root, craft a slimeball and put a spare crop where Gary can take it.
steps.note: Repeated cut at 04:43, turned fresh top into one slimeball and stocked it and previous crop. Gary confirmed receipt of his separate starter.

history.name: Smelt workshop ore with wind
history.goal: Send iron grit from the existing Enrichment Chamber into a wind-powered Energized Smelter and collect a batch at the east workshop.
history.why: Neighbours can turn mining trips into usable ingots while working elsewhere, without tending coal.
history.done_when: Three raw iron produce four ingots with wind power and the chamber-to-smelter transfer running without hand carrying grit. Verify the finished batch and explain the inputs and outputs at the bench.
history.needs: Working wind line, four steel, four infused alloys, three osmium or two circuits and one osmium, six glass and an accessible item transfer face.
history.evidence: Loaded exactly 3 raw iron into the empty Chamber. Its slots cleared through an allowlisted Importer and downward Exporter. Rear wind smelter showed 2 grit and 2 ingots, then 4 ingots and no grit, without hand carrying or fuel. Collected and deposited four ingots for Gary. Front sign and facility #4 describe access.
history.unlocks: Shared wind-powered ore batches from Chamber to rear smelter, four ingots per three raw iron.

steps.text: Check workshop stock and gather the missing sand, osmium and iron.
steps.note: Gary added 3 raw iron, verified in person. Gathered workshop glass and osmium; smelter already built.

steps.text: Make and power an Energized Smelter beside the chamber or join them with item transport.
steps.note: Installed Energized Smelter in rear wall and two Universal Cables. Power gauge full, no power item in machine.

steps.text: Set and test item transfer on a small iron batch.
steps.note: An allowlisted Importer at the Chamber output and a downward filtered Exporter sent all four IE iron grit into the wind smelter automatically.

steps.text: Verify four ingots from three raw iron and make the working route available.
steps.note: Counted four output ingots, deposited all four for Gary in the workshop supply chest and verified a wall sign and shared method.

history.name: Breed pigs at the west bank
history.goal: Start a shared breeding herd by the stream
history.why: A fenced breeding pair gives the settlement renewable food once the herd grows
history.done_when: Two live adult pigs are together behind the closed gate, breeding consumes feed and yields a visible piglet, and a planted root crop is available for later feed.
history.needs: A carrot, potato, or beetroot and two adult pigs within luring distance.
history.evidence: Gary established four potato starts and helped return the herd. Two potatoes fed to two adults produced two visible piglets, growing time 1,199 seconds. I counted four adults and two piglets inside after both gates were visibly shut.
history.unlocks: The potato patch supplies a repeatable breeding pair. Gary shares the west pen with two adult breeders reserved.

steps.text: Scout two pigs and finish a lit pen with a working gate.
steps.note: Both gates are tested and on cobblestone footings. Gary returned the surviving adult and three piglets; all four still inside after I shut both.

steps.text: Plant a root crop and reserve two feed items after replanting.
steps.note: Gary’s four planted potato crops are visible by the stream. Took two reserve potatoes from his pantry for recovery.

steps.text: Lure two adults into the pen and close the gate.
steps.note: Four adults inside, both gates manually closed on stone supports. Outer gate now at x86.

steps.text: Feed both adults and verify a piglet.
steps.note: Two spare potatoes fed to separate adults; two new piglets appeared. Counted six safely penned after closing both gates.

history.name: Bring the chicken flock home
history.goal: Make and stock a roofed west-bank chicken coop with a reliable entry.
history.why: Eggs give the settlement renewable food and pancake ingredients. A reliable shared flock saves both Gary and me trips looking for strays.
history.done_when: Two adults and their new chick are seen inside the closed roofed coop after both keepers leave. A neighbour knows the approach and how to keep birds in.
history.needs: An open level shelf, covered barrier, manual two-stage entry, one held bird, one roaming adult, seeds.
history.evidence: Gary brought a second adult. I fed the pair, observed their new chick and counted all three again from outside with both doors closed. Gary used and secured the north approach; shared marker and facility describe the door routine.
history.unlocks: Renewable chicken breeding and eggs at the west-bank coop, with seed and egg storage at the entrance.

steps.text: Walk the old pen and choose a nearby shelf clear of Gary’s pasture.
steps.note: Picked the open birch shelf south of the stream crop, east of the old pasture. It keeps the coop entrance on a separate path and close to where the roaming chicken was seen.

steps.text: Build, light and check a roofed coop with a manual two-stage entry.
steps.note: Roof and windows finished. Lit room, vestibule and entry. I walked through and closed both doors separately; the inner and outer handles work from either side.

steps.text: Bring in Gary’s held chicken and a second adult. Feed and verify a chick.
steps.note: Fed both adults inside the closed coop and observed the third chicken plus the breeding advancement.

steps.text: Watch from outside with entry shut and share the coop approach.
steps.note: Closed both doors on exit, then confirmed all three chickens inside. Gary used the entry; the shared marker and facility carry the approach and door rule.

history.name: Make searchable workshop storage
history.goal: Enable shared searchable storage at the East workshop using its wind supply.
history.why: Neighbours can find and exchange workshop materials in one place. A powered network opens later processing automation.
history.done_when: Wind powers a Controller, Grid and 1k Storage Block. Deposit and retrieve a real item, verify it survives a brief disconnect, and share access.
history.needs: Quartz, glowstone, iron, redstone, gold, glass, stone, silicon, processor parts, one diamond and a sheltered powered cable face.
history.evidence: Wind kept the Controller powered with a Grid and 1k Storage Block attached. Both deposited stacks reappeared after a Controller redstone disable and recovery. The filtered Exporter sent four saplings to its chest; quick-move took them into inventory as the two stone stayed in storage. Access and output are shared in facility #9 and in town chat.
history.unlocks: Neighbours can deposit bulk supplies, view contents and send selected supplies to an ordinary chest. Direct Grid search and result clicks via resident client are still under investigation.

steps.text: Bring Nether materials to the workshop and count parts and power access.
steps.note: Verified 26 quartz and 6 glowstone in workshop chest with 4 smelted/2 raw iron, 17 redstone, 10 gold and 3 cables. Active wind cable at 40 kJ. East cable face can branch above the machines.

steps.text: Prepare and smelt processor and storage ingredients. Gather shortages from existing routes.
steps.note: Made a binding batch from hand-harvested kelp and smelted basic, improved and advanced processors. Grid and 1k block built.

steps.text: Assemble the Controller, Grid and 1k Storage Block on a sheltered branch of the workshop power line.
steps.note: Placed the Controller, Grid and 1k Storage Block adjacent on the roofed East workshop bench.

steps.text: Test real deposits, retrieval and reconnect recovery. Share access and record what works.
steps.note: Four deposited saplings returned through filtered output chest; two stone stayed. Both stocks survived Controller off/on. Shared access and client controls recorded in facility #9.

history.name: Open a quartz and glowstone route
history.goal: Establish a dependable Nether route for workshop quartz and glowstone.
history.why: These materials let us build a searchable shared store for the workshop's growing output.
history.done_when: Bring back at least 24 quartz and 4 glowstone dust through the same protected portal and record the way and access for neighbours.
history.needs: Portal access, building blocks and light, food, gold armour, iron tools and an exit marker.
history.evidence: Carried 26 quartz and six glowstone dust through the same paired frames. Closed both doors and verified the route back from the covered landing via railed bridge, forest torch line and birch portal door. Shared fork, bridge and landing waypoints and access record in facility #7.
history.unlocks: Workshop materials for first Refined Storage system and repeatable Nether runs with a guarded approach.

steps.text: Find an offered portal or prepare a protected route to frame materials.
steps.note: Gary opened a dry lava draw bay with a stone lip. He cast the first verified obsidian at the protected portal room.

steps.text: Ready a travel kit and verify departure and arrival points.
steps.note: Verified both directions between Shore vestibule and independent Warped terrace frame. Returned through the new pair at full health.

steps.text: Mark a covered route from the portal and gather quartz and glowstone.
steps.note: 26 quartz banked via portal. East terrace reaches a railed bridge, lit netherrack bore and guarded glowstone landing; six dust collected. Verified both ways from bore to bridge approach.

steps.text: Return with supplies and leave an access record.
steps.note: Returned portal to shore with six dust, reunited with 26 quartz previously carried through. Saved shared waypoints, signed bridge, and dated note on facility #7.
